person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: null-result
span.quote: However, when generalization requires systematic compositional skills (as in the “dax” example above), RNNs fail spectacularly.

span.label: systematic compositional generalization in sequence-to-sequence networks
span.quote: We thus use it to test a wide range of modern recurrent network architectures in terms of their compositional abilities.

span.label: simulation
span.quote: Using the seq2seq framework, we tested a range of standard recurrent neural network models from the literature: simple recurrent networks (SRNs; Elman, 1990), long short-term memory networks (LSTMs; Hochreiter & Schmidhuber, 1997), and gated recurrent units (GRUs; Chung et al., 2014).

span.label: the SCAN benchmark grammar lacks recursion and generates only a finite command set
span.quote: The SCAN grammar, lacking recursion, generates a finite but large set of unambiguous commands (20,910, to be precise).

span.label: The machine-translation demonstration is small-scale and its result is described by the authors as preliminary.
span.quote: Although this is a small-scale machine translation problem, our preliminary result suggests that models will similarly struggle with systematic compositionality in larger data sets, when adding a new word to their vocabulary, in ways that people clearly do not.

span.label: The authors concede the Experiment 3 setup (a primitive seen only in isolation) may be unfairly opaque for a computational model that has no evidence the new action belongs to the same class as the others.
span.quote: Although we suspect humans would not have problems with this setup, it arguably is too opaque for a computational model, which could lack evidence for “jumping” being the same sort of action as “walking”.

span.label: The benchmark's name is an acronym whose first letter is its own admission of simplification.
span.quote: We call our data set SCAN because it is a Simplified version of the CommAI Navigation tasks

span.label: The criterion the models are measured against comes from an argument the authors call controversial.
span.quote: In a set of influential and controversial papers, Jerry Fodor and other researchers have argued that neural networks are not plausible models of the mind because they are associative devices that cannot capture systematic compositionality

span.label: Failure is defined by what an idealised agent would find trivial, not by a measured human baseline.
span.quote: However, the models are catastrophically affected by systematic differences between training and test sentences, of the sort that would be trivial for an agent equipped with an “algebraic mind

span.label: SCAN - AN ACRONYM THAT ADMITS ITS OWN REDUCTION: the S is for Simplified, because the data set is a simplified version of the CommAI Navigation tasks; the expansion carries the scope limitation and the four letters that get cited do not
span.quote: We call our data set SCAN because it is a Simplified version of the CommAI Navigation tasks

span.label: systematic compositionality - A CONTESTED PHILOSOPHICAL CRITERION USED AS A BENCHMARK: it comes from papers the authors themselves call influential and controversial, in which neural networks are argued to be associative devices that cannot capture it, so a SCAN score inherits an argument it cannot display
span.quote: In a set of influential and controversial papers, Jerry Fodor and other researchers have argued that neural networks are not plausible models of the mind because they are associative devices that cannot capture systematic compositionality

span.label: a catastrophic failure - RELATIVE TO AN ALGEBRAIC MIND: the models' errors are called catastrophic because the differences involved would be trivial for an agent equipped with an algebraic mind, which is a construct rather than a measured comparison group
span.quote: However, the models are catastrophically affected by systematic differences between training and test sentences, of the sort that would be trivial for an agent equipped with an “algebraic mind

span.label: builds-on → sequence-to-sequence learning methods
span.quote: This problem is naturally framed as a sequence-to-sequence task, and, due to its simplicity, it is ideal to study systematic generalization to novel examples in a controlled setup.

span.label: builds-on → the CommAI Navigation tasks (Mikolov et al., 2016)
span.quote: We call our data set SCAN because it is a Simplified version of the CommAI Navigation tasks (Mikolov et al., 2016).

span.label: builds-on → the attentional sequence-to-sequence model of Bahdanau et al. (2015)
span.quote: Recurrent networks with attention have become increasingly popular in the last few years, and thus we also tested each network with and without an attentional mechanism, using the model from Bahdanau et al. (2015) (see Supplementary for more details).

span.label: extends → three decades of prior tests of compositional generalization in neural networks in the systematicity debate
span.quote: However, to the best of our knowledge, ours is the first study testing systematicity in modern seq2seq models, and our results confirm the mixed picture.
